raw_response:
I farm these 12 mu myself, and after 30 years I still mostly trust what I have seen on my own land. In Quzhou, wheat-maize is the steady way. One crop supports the next, and if I disturb that rhythm, I lose time and money. I finished with wheat and maize many years already, so I will not make big changes this year. The extension man usually talks about balanced fertilizer, and I listen, but on my fields I still do a little by experience. Wheat cannot be starved, otherwise tillers are weak and yield drops. Maize after wheat has a very tight window, so I keep the land preparation simple and plant fast. I have a well, so I will use water when it matters, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times unless the season turns dry. Some people from my family work off-farm, so I mainly rely on family labor for key days and try not to create extra work.
